sections.h2: What does the Will County Recorder of Deeds do for a home seller?
sections.html:
The Will County Recorder of Deeds is the office that puts a deed on the public record after a sale in Will County. It sits at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, and the phone is (815) 740-4637. The recorder's price list covers standard documents, uniform commercial code filings, plats, state and federal documents and certified copies, so a deed is just one of several filings the counter handles.

Will County is the fourth most populous county in Illinois, with 696,355 residents in the 2020 census and Joliet as the seat. Its cities and villages include Joliet, Naperville, Bolingbrook and Plainfield, and a deed for any parcel in the county is recorded at this one office.

The recorder's site also points customers to Fidlar products such as Official Records Online, Laredo and Tapestry, which are the platforms used for searching and submitting records.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Will County?
sections.html:
A standard document costs $90.00 to record. That schedule took effect October 1, 2025 under Public Act 103-0884 and County Resolution 25-224, which the Will County Board approved on August 21, 2025. Every document received on or after that date falls under it.

Will County recording fee schedule effective October 1, 2025, Will County Recorder
Document typeFee
Standard document$90.00
Standard document, RHSP exempt$71.00
Non-standard document$118.00
Non-standard document, RHSP exempt$99.00
Uniform Commercial Code filing$73.00
UCC termination$60.00
Plat document (subdivision or condo)$144.00
State and federal documents$71.00
Certified copy$42.00

The recording fee is separate from the transfer tax and from any fee the title company charges for preparing and submitting the deed.

sections.h2: What makes a document standard for Will County recording?
sections.html:
The recorder prices a document as standard when it meets the paper and layout rules in state law, and when it contains a limited number of references.

  • One or more sheets measuring 8.5 by 11 inches, not permanently bound and not a continuous form.
  • Black ink, typed, printed or handwritten, with signatures and dates allowed in contrasting colors if they reproduce clearly.
  • White paper of at least 20-pound weight, with clean margins of at least one-half inch on the top, bottom and each side.
  • A blank space of at least 3 by 5 inches in the upper right corner of the first page.
  • No staples or attachments affixed to any page.
  • Up to five Property Identification Number references and up to five related document number references.

Graphic displays that come with a document may measure up to 11 by 17 inches without an added charge. A document that does not conform is recorded only after the extra fee is paid.

sections.h2: When does Will County treat a deed as non-standard?
sections.html:
The $118.00 fee applies to anything that fails the standard test. The recorder's schedule names three common triggers.

  • A legal-size (8.5 by 14) page, unless the page is an exhibit drawing or plat.
  • Six or more Property Identification Number references.
  • Six or more related document number references.

Plats filed as stand-alone documents also fall in this class when they are at least 11 by 17 inches and no larger than 30 by 36 inches. That covers miscellaneous plats, easements and dedications.

A deed for a house on a single parcel usually passes as standard if the title company prints it correctly. A deed that bundles several lots, or a deed with a long list of prior documents, is where the higher fee can appear. Ask the title agent to count the parcel numbers before the filing goes in.

sections.h2: What is the RHSP surcharge on a Will County recording?
sections.html:
The $90.00 and $118.00 fees include a $19.00 Rental Housing Support Program surcharge. The schedule says that surcharge does not apply to documents recorded by federal, state or local government agencies, which is why the exempt rates are $71.00 and $99.00.

A private home sale deed pays the full rate. The exempt rows matter for agencies and for state and federal filings, which the office lists at $71.00. If you are unsure whether the filer counts as a government body, ask the recorder's office before the submission so the check is written for the right amount.

sections.h2: How does the Illinois transfer tax work on a Will County sale?
sections.html:
Illinois charges a tax on the privilege of transferring title, set at 50 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, stated in the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). When the deed says the property goes subject to a mortgage, the outstanding mortgage amount does not count toward the base.

The tax is due whether or not a document is recorded, and it applies to transfers made through one or more related transactions. The recorder collects it by selling revenue stamps (35 ILCS 200/31-15). The statute set a phase-out of paper stamps by December 31, 2025, after which counties issue electronic stamps or alternative indicia, and each recordation is sent to the Illinois Department of Revenue through its electronic system.

Ask the title company which party pays under the contract and how it appears on the settlement statement. Ask the Recorder and your municipality whether any local transfer tax applies as well.

sections.h2: Which deeds are exempt from the Illinois transfer tax?
sections.html:
The exemption list in 35 ILCS 200/31-45 is short and specific. Several entries matter to homeowners and heirs.

  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Deeds that confirm, correct, modify or supplement a deed already recorded, without more consideration.
  • Tax deeds.
  • Deeds that release property held as security for a debt.
  • Deeds of partition.
  • Deeds issued to a mortgage holder in a foreclosure or in a transfer in lieu of foreclosure.

Some exempt deeds still need the declaration filed. The statute says so for certain governmental, charitable and exchange deeds, so an exemption does not always mean skipping the form.

sections.h2: What steps put a deed on record in Will County after closing?
sections.html:
Most sales close through a title company, which prepares the deed and sends it to the recorder, so the seller seldom goes to the counter. For a sale outside a title company, such as a family transfer, follow the steps yourself.

  1. Confirm the deed uses the standard layout, including the 3 by 5 inch blank space on the first page.
  2. List each Property Identification Number and keep the count at five or fewer if you want the standard fee.
  3. Complete the transfer declaration and work out the transfer tax with the recorder.
  4. Pay the recording fee and any tax, then keep the stamped copy or the confirmation.
  5. Order a certified copy if a lender or court needs one, at $42.00.

Before the deed goes in, clear the property tax side with the county Treasurer. Unpaid installments stay attached to the parcel and bear interest by state law, so a payoff letter protects the new owner and the seller.

faqs.q: How much does the Will County Recorder charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A standard document is $90.00, and a non-standard one is $118.00, under the schedule effective October 1, 2025. The exempt rates are $71.00 and $99.00.

faqs.q: Where is the Will County Recorder of Deeds office?
faqs.a: The office is at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, and the phone is (815) 740-4637. The site is willcountyrecorder.com.

faqs.q: How is the Illinois transfer tax figured in Will County?
faqs.a: The rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the transfer declaration. A mortgage the buyer takes the property subject to is left out of the base.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed exempt from the transfer tax?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The list in 35 ILCS 200/31-45 exempts deeds with consideration under $100, correction deeds and certain others. A deed with a stated value above those limits follows the normal rule.

faqs.q: How much is a certified copy from the Will County Recorder?
faqs.a: A certified copy costs $42.00 under the current schedule. Call the office before you order, since fees can change by county resolution.
